court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: City ordinance regulating bill-posting and requiring permission to erect large bill-boards was a valid exercise of the police power and within the city's charter authority.
notes: Bill-posting/billboard licensing ordinance case; no connection to lodging, boarding, or short-term dwelling letting.

court: New York County Court, Franklin County
holding_summary: Summary proceedings to remove a holding-over tenant were reversed for defective notice to quit, jury competency issues, and improper hearsay evidence.
notes: Ordinary landlord-tenant summary proceedings over a leased farm/dwelling with a multi-year written lease; not about short-term room letting, lodgers, or boarding-house regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Lessee of a restaurant/gambling resort was denied an injunction against continuous police surveillance of the premises, on unclean-hands grounds.
notes: Restaurant/gambling-house police-surveillance injunction case; no lodging or boarding-house issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A lessee who left an associate's property on leased business premises after the term expired was held over as matter of law, absent a new surrender agreement.
notes: Commercial-premises holding-over dispute involving a business tenant (electric railway systems company); not a lodging/boarding letting case.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Conviction for holding an unlicensed 'exhibition' was reversed because free demonstrations used to sell a book did not constitute an 'exhibition' within the licensing ordinance.
notes: Municipal licensing of 'exhibitions'/amusements ordinance case; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Use-and-occupation recovery was sustained against an occupant of a dwelling despite an outstanding lease to a third person, because the occupant was presumptively an assignee of the term.
notes: Whole-dwelling tenancy/assignment-of-lease dispute at a monthly rent over roughly a year; not about short-term room letting, lodgers, or boarding-house practice.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A complaint styled as one for use and occupation of extra store space beyond a written lease actually sounded in trespass, since no landlord-tenant relation was shown as to that space.
notes: Commercial store-space trespass/use-and-occupation pleading dispute; no lodging or boarding element.

holding_summary: On a note action, the court allowed evidence, under a general denial, that a counterclaimed board debt was actually owed to and paid to a third party who ran the boarding house, not the defendant.
notes: Evidentiary/pleading dispute over a promissory note and a counterclaim for board; the identity of the boarding-house keeper is incidental to the note litigation, and the opinion states no doctrine on the character or regulation of boarding-house letting itself.

holding_summary: In a tax-title and mortgage-foreclosure ejectment dispute, a daughter's possession of the family home (in which boarders were kept) was too equivocal to give the mortgagee constructive notice of her unrecorded deed.
notes: Tax-title/mortgage-foreclosure land title dispute; the fact that the family 'kept boarders in the house' is mentioned only as evidence bearing on notice from possession, not litigated as a lodging/boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A lease/grant of agricultural land for lives, reserving rent, is not void ab initio under the constitutional 12-year limit but is valid only for the first 12 years.
notes: Constitutional limitation on the term of agricultural land leases; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A liquor tax certificate is personal property that can be the subject of a chattel mortgage, so its fraudulent surrender by the mortgagor violated the Penal Code.
notes: Chattel-mortgage fraud prosecution concerning a liquor tax certificate; no lodging/boarding content.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A landlord's notice of increased rent, served on a tenant's wife only after the new term had already begun, was too late to charge the tenant with the higher rent.
notes: Rent-increase notice dispute tied to a pending real-estate exchange, involving occupancy of a single-family dwelling at nominal rent; not a lodging/boarding letting case.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A written lease of a house 'to be used for furnished room house only' could be shown by parol to have been made and knowingly permitted for the unlawful purpose of running a house of prostitution, and evidence that the lessor operated other such houses through housekeepers was admissible on his intent, defeating his action for rent.

quotes.text: the purpose of the tenancy created by it, as expressed therein, was that the house was “to be used for furnished room house only.”
The keeping of such a house was a misdemeanor at common law, as was the demise of a house with intent that it be kept, and which was kept, for such purpose.
From the facts so found, the consequence would necessarily be the-defeat of the action upon the lease.
the plaintiff had other houses in that vicinity, in which he, through his housekeepers, was conducting.

notes: Head lease of an entire house for use as a 'furnished room house' turned out to be a house of prostitution operated by the tenant with the owner's knowledge; owner also ran similar houses elsewhere through housekeepers. Duration of any individual room occupancies is not stated in the opinion — only the four-year head lease term is given — so duration is marked unclear.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A village ordinance imposing a daily license fee on nonresident sample-sellers was void as an unauthorized revenue tax and discriminatory restraint of trade, not a valid police-power license.
notes: Peddler/sample-sales licensing ordinance case; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
holding_summary: An executor's power to sell land for distribution did not vest title in him, so he could not maintain ejectment against a grantee who held fee title under a prior family assignment.
notes: Ejectment/will-construction dispute over title to a house and lot; no lodging or boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
holding_summary: A conviction for receiving stolen bonds was affirmed; evidence of altered bond numbers and disputed handwriting testimony on powers of attorney was properly admitted for the jury to weigh.
notes: Criminal appeal concerning receipt of stolen bonds and expert handwriting/notary evidence; no lodging/boarding content.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A depositor's complaint against a bank for dishonoring a check need not allege indorsement where the bank's outright repudiation of its debt to the depositor excused that formality.
notes: Bank check-dishonor pleading case; a boarding-house keeper's anticipatory-breach rule is cited only as an analogy among several examples of the general contract-repudiation doctrine, not litigated on these facts.

holding_summary: The court declined to overturn an excise board rule requiring surrender of an existing liquor license before issuance of a new storekeeper's license, finding the rule not arbitrary.
notes: Liquor license certiorari proceeding under the Excise Law; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house regulation.
